speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the Ministry is studying the policies and rules governing the use of e-scooters in Berlin and Paris; and (b) whether Paris' move to ban e-scooters from footpaths can be emulated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: This is my last question on personal mobility devices (PMDs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: There is a wide range of practices across jurisdictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We have to tailor our approach to our local context and the needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In Singapore, such active mobility devices are useful for short journeys within towns and as first- and last-mile options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We have also put in place a comprehensive set of regulations, with regular enforcement by Land Transport Authority (LTA) enforcement officers at hotspots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We encourage members of public as well as the vast majority of responsible PMD users to help spot and report errant riders to LTA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Collectively, we can encourage safe riding and considerate behaviour on our shared paths.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It looks like LTA or the Ministry of Transport is very fixated on the thinking.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think by allowing PMD and e-scooters on the footpaths, you are shifting more risks to the pedestrians.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Yes, you can report, you can take enforcement action but how many officers do you have to take enforcement action?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My question is, what is LTA's advice to all pedestrians, especially the elderly, the pregnant women and the children for sharing footpaths with the e-scooters?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have already one case of a man who suffered brain injury after being hit at Marina Bay.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And yesterday, I just received an email from my resident after being hit by an e-scooter on the footpath a year ago.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have another resident who was molested along the footpath by an e-scooter rider.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Police could not do anything because it was at night.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask what advice the Senior Minister of State would give to pedestrians in order for them to be safe.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The reason we reduced the speed limit is so that we can enhance the safety by increasing the amount of time for PMD users as well as pedestrians to react to unforeseen circumstances.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With this lowered speed limit, we also hope that the severity of injuries, should they occur, would be much lower.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Of course, we do not hope for accidents to occur, but we hope that with the lower speed limit, we have enough reaction time to react to any unforeseen circumstances.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also have to exercise alertness whenever there are any PMD users approaching us.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For the PMD users, they are advised to ride carefully within the speed limit allowed, as well as to slow down when faced with a crowd in front of them.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These are some commonsense practices that PMD users should exercise.
